copy.headline: Trump says extensive oil exploration is coming in Greenland

extended.text: Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social, his social network, on Wednesday morning that 'extensive exploration of oil, gas and minerals' was being prepared 'in our new and beautiful Greenland'. It is unclear which surveys he means.

The Foreign Ministry told Ritzau that any American exploration must follow Greenlandic law, because Greenland's self-government has taken over raw materials from Denmark. The agreement of 22 September between Greenland, Denmark and the US does not change that, it said.
But the ministry also confirmed to Jyllands-Posten that the American government can block other countries' investments in Greenland, India's as well as China's and Russia's.

Jørgen Hammeken-Holm, permanent secretary in Greenland's department for business and raw materials, told CNN that American companies are active but 'very far from a massive exploration'. It can take years, he said, before the many smaller explorations become operational.

Aleqa Hammond, chair of Siumut, a Greenlandic social-democratic party, told Berlingske that no company or country will ever get free access to Greenland's underground. The agreement must still be approved by the countries' parliaments.

short.text: Donald Trump wrote on Wednesday that extensive exploration of oil, gas and minerals was being prepared in Greenland. The Foreign Ministry says any American exploration must follow Greenlandic law, and a senior Greenlandic official told CNN that activity is 'very far from a massive exploration'.

copy.headline: Danish land registry limits searches after 17.2 million in a few days

standard.text: Denmark's digital land registry has limited the number of searches it accepts after receiving 17.2 million in a few days, the Danish Court Administration said in a statement on Wednesday. It normally gets fewer than two million a week.

The searches were legal and touched only records open to anyone without a login. 'It is the number of look-ups that gives cause for attention,' said Rikke Holler, president of the Land Registration Court.

The agency names no cause but warns that the records could make fraud attempts more credible, citing the recent leak of 8.8 million CPR numbers, Denmark's personal identification numbers. The justice minister is briefing parliament.

short.text: Denmark's digital land registry has limited searches after receiving 17.2 million in a few days, against fewer than two million in a normal week, the Danish Court Administration said on Wednesday. The searches were legal, but it warns the records could make fraud more credible.

copy.headline: Ukrainian accused of blowing up Nord Stream stays silent as his trial opens

standard.text: Serhii Kuznetsov, a former Ukrainian special forces officer, will not give evidence at his trial, his lawyer said as it opened in Hamburg on Wednesday. Prosecutors accuse him of leading the team that blew up the Nord Stream gas pipelines between Russia and Germany in September 2022, and charge him as an accessory to war crimes. The trial is expected to end in February.

Nicola Canestrini, his lawyer, says no clear evidence links him to the blasts and that Russia used the pipelines as a weapon, so the case should be dismissed. 'Is it illegal to destroy an aggressor's infrastructure without harming anyone?' he asked the court.

short.text: Serhii Kuznetsov, a former Ukrainian special forces officer accused of leading the sabotage of the Nord Stream gas pipelines in September 2022, will not give evidence at his trial, which opened in Hamburg on Wednesday. His lawyer wants the case dismissed.

copy.headline_short: Nord Stream trial opens in Hamburg

copy.headline: Ukraine's president says he feels betrayed by Trump

standard.text: Asked by Piers Morgan, a British television presenter, whether he felt betrayed by Donald Trump, Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukraine's president, answered on Wednesday: 'Actually, yes. But it is more complex than just my feelings.'

Trump has said in recent days that Zelensky should be replaced, and has agreed a diesel deal with Russia that has been criticised for giving Moscow money for the war. Ukraine's military has also had its access to Starlink, Elon Musk's satellite network, squeezed.

'If you stand in the middle, you have to stay in the middle. Not on the wrong side,' Zelensky said. He blamed Trump's advisers. He spoke in London, where he was visiting Andy Burnham, the British prime minister.

copy.headline: Two parties want the nitrogen law delayed after a university's calculation error

standard.text: Venstre, a liberal party, and Liberal Alliance, a libertarian party, want the nitrogen law delayed by half a year after Aarhus University admitted errors in the calculations behind the law's discharge limits. The law is due to take effect after new year.

The university announced the error on Tuesday, having said the previous week that it had double-checked its figures after criticism from Seges, agriculture's think tank. Because of the error, some farmers would have been allowed to discharge less nitrogen than they should.
Christian Rabjerg Madsen, the minister for nature and animal welfare, told Ritzau in a written comment: 'I take that very seriously, and it must of course be put right.'

short.text: Venstre, a liberal party, and Liberal Alliance, a libertarian party, want the nitrogen law delayed by half a year after Aarhus University admitted errors in the calculations behind its limits on farmers' nitrogen discharges.

copy.headline_short: Parties seek delay to nitrogen law
copy.deck: Aarhus University has apologised for the mistake; the minister says it must be put right.

copy.headline: Party says a citizenship applicant praised Hamas and wants her questioned

standard.text: Liberal Alliance, a libertarian party, wants a woman who is due to receive Danish citizenship called before the naturalisation committee of the Folketing, Denmark's parliament. The party says its own screening of the 2,055 people on the citizenship bill found that she had repeatedly praised Hamas and its former leaders Yahya Sinwar and Ismail Haniyeh.
She denies it. 'I do not support anyone who kills anyone,' she told Politiken, and said she would attend.

The government decided to put the bill forward before a model for screening applicants for anti-democratic views is ready. Dansk Folkeparti, a nationalist party, backs the summons; Enhedslisten, a far-left party, calls it undignified.

short.text: Liberal Alliance, a libertarian party, wants a parliamentary committee to question a woman on a bill granting citizenship to 2,055 people, saying she praised Hamas. She denies supporting Hamas and says she will attend.
